title: I made a UE5 horror demo with an AI agent writing most of the code. Here's how the workflow ended up
author: sargetun123
selftext:
Just put out a free demo of Buried Kin, a first person horror game set in an old psych hospital. I wanted to share how it was built because AI did a lot of the heavy lifting, but not in the way people usually picture it.

I came up with the story, the setting and how it should play, and I did all the playtesting. An AI coding agent (Claude) wrote most of the C++ for Unreal 5, plus the Python scripts that build the levels inside the editor. So rooms, doors and props get placed by scripts instead of by hand, which made it easy to rebuild a whole level after a change.

The biggest thing that made it work was testing. The agent set up automated runs that play through the critical path, take screenshots and check logs, so every fix got checked before I played it. My job turned into playing it, writing down what felt wrong or broken, and approving or rejecting each fix one by one. Some of the 3D props came from Tripo, and the menu music was AI generated. The breathing and sound effects are real recordings.

It's not hands-off. Some bugs took a lot of back and forth, and the AI is great at code but needs a human to say "this feels wrong." Still, I don't think I could have built this solo otherwise.

Demo is free on itch, about 20 to 30 min, Windows: [https://sargetun.itch.io/buried-kin-demo](https://sargetun.itch.io/buried-kin-demo)

Happy to answer questions about the workflow.
